teams.heading: Italy prop Simone Ferrari rates improved Fiji no easier than Argentina
teams.body: Asked in Udine whether Saturday's Nations Championship meeting would be easier than last weekend's 14-19 home defeat to Argentina, Italy prop Simone Ferrari answered flatly that it would not. He described Fiji as an improved, solid side on the rise, with many players based in France and plenty of physicality. Ferrari called Italy's scrum a well-honed weapon and wants the Azzurri to match the intensity they showed against Argentina. Fiji arrive after a 15-43 defeat to Ireland.

teams.heading: Five-try wing Will Joseph in line to start against New Zealand
teams.body: Gloucester's Will Joseph is understood to be in pole position to keep the wing berth for Saturday's Nations Championship meeting with the All Blacks, with wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso ruled out of the autumn by an ankle injury. Last weekend's 78-15 win over Japan was only Joseph's second cap, four and a half years after his debut against Australia in July 2022, and he became the fifth England men's player to score five tries in one match. Cadan Murley, the squad's other specialist wing, is his rival for the spot.

teams.heading: Matthieu Jalibert steers France at fly-half in first training run before Argentina
teams.body: Rugbyrama's report from Tuesday's first full session at Marcoussis found one certainty: the fly-half will run France's game against the Pumas, restoring a conventional halves pairing after the improvisation that put captain Antoine Dupont at 10 against South Africa. Dupont was back at scrum-half in a near-unchanged backline, though outside back Aaron Grandidier-Nkanang was spared and his Pau teammate Grégoire Arfeuil took his place. Bib swaps among the forwards threw up surprises. France must beat Argentina to be sure of a place in the Nations Championship final in London.

teams.heading: Sam Prendergast cleared to face Springboks after hip-drop citing is dismissed
teams.body: The fly-half had faced a potential ban for a tackle on Fiji captain Peceli Yato in last Saturday's 43-15 win. He was cited under a new offence added to Law 9.13 this month. At Tuesday's hearing, an independent committee unanimously threw the case out after evidence from the 23-year-old and submissions from Ireland head coach Andy Farrell, leaving him available for Saturday's Nations Championship test. South Africa head coach Rassie Erasmus, now serving a six-match ban, had predicted Prendergast would escape punishment "on a technicality" while condemning the tackle itself.

lead.why: Ireland's first-choice fly-half had a citing thrown out and is available for the Springboks, a fresh event about Ireland.

teams.heading: Italy chase first Nations Championship win against Fiji with series level six-all
teams.body: Head coach Gonzalo Quesada's Italy face a Fiji side who, like them, are still looking for a first win in the competition. Both sit bottom of their respective pools going into Saturday's Round 6 test in Udine. The 12 previous meetings have split six wins apiece, and the last, in November 2017, went Italy's way 19-10 in Catania. Fiji arrive off a defeat by Ireland in Dublin, where they were held scoreless in the second half. OnRugby rates it likely the two meet again on the final weekend in London.

teams.heading: Scotland lose Tuipulotu, White, Dempsey and Cummings to injury before Japan test
teams.body: Captain Sione Tuipulotu, a late withdrawal from Sunday's 15-12 win over Australia with a knee injury, returns to his club with three men hurt in that game: Toulon scrum-half Ben White (knee), number eight Jack Dempsey (foot) and Glasgow lock Scott Cummings (leg). Head coach Gregor Townsend has called up Edinburgh forwards Grant Gilchrist and Magnus Bradbury plus Leicester lock Cam Henderson. Uncapped Glasgow back Josh McKay qualifies on residency this week and could debut against Japan at Murrayfield.

teams.heading: Steve Tandy credits Dewi Lake's half-time words for Wales' second-half blitz
teams.body: Wales head coach Steve Tandy says he still feels emotional and proud after last Saturday's 35-28 win over New Zealand. The All Blacks scored with the last move of the first half after a Wales attack, yet Tandy said nobody in the changing room felt it had to be the turning point: Dewi Lake's words were electrifying, and two tries followed in the first nine minutes after the restart. He also hailed the defence under coaches Dan Lydiate and Peter Murchie ahead of another very tough test against Australia this weekend.

lead.why: Fresh Wales head coach comments on the half-time turning point, which earlier editions have not covered.

teams.heading: Bautista Bernasconi steps up from Argentina XV to score in Genoa win
teams.body: Picked for the Argentina XV rather than the Pumas, the Benetton hooker started last Saturday's 19-14 win over Italy only because Julián Montoya, Ignacio Ruiz and Leonel Oviedo were all injured, then scored from a maul as Argentina levelled at 7-7 by half-time. The casualty list runs deeper: Thomas Gallo, Santiago Grondona, Marcos Kremer and Joaquín Oviedo are also injured, and with Santiago Carreras and Juan Cruz Mallía both out, Bautista Delguy moved to fly-half during Tomás Albornoz's sin-bin spell.

teams.heading: Planet Rugby column questions Les Kiss's authority after Wallabies' Murrayfield defeat
teams.body: Wallabies head coach Les Kiss is clearly useful, Planet Rugby's columnist allows — but as a specialist or assistant, not the man in charge. Watching Kiss speak after Sunday's 15-12 Nations Championship loss to Scotland at Murrayfield, the writer saw nothing to suggest he has the standing to sell a vision to the team or the Australian public. Nor, the piece argues, will 'sugar-hits' such as Sydney Roosters pair Mark Nawaqanitawase and Angus Crichton heading to union fix a side that needs forwards and a reliable fly-half.

lead.why: A direct challenge to Les Kiss's standing as head coach is the sharpest Australia story not yet run on this tab.

teams.heading: Moriyama and Brua returned home injured before Japan's Twickenham defeat to England
teams.body: Rugby Asia 247 reported on 12 November, two days before the England match, that squad member Miu Austin Moriyama and left wing Inoke Brua had returned to Japan with injuries. Faulua Makisi of Kubota Spears and Jone Naikabra of Toshiba Brave Lupus were called up as replacements. Brua's wing berth went to another Toshiba man, Rinku Tokito, selected by head coach Eddie Jones to make his debut in a side that went on to lose 15-78 at Twickenham.

teams.heading: Will Jordan reportedly ahead of schedule to face England at Twickenham
teams.body: All Blacks wing Will Jordan has reportedly completed another training session, with Italian outlet OnRugby saying his recovery has been quicker than expected and that a start against England on Saturday would be no surprise. Jordan missed the 28-35 defeat to Wales in Cardiff with an injury picked up against Scotland. The BBC also places him in head coach Dave Rennie's selection mix, alongside the confirmed returns of Damian McKenzie, Jordie Barrett, Codie Taylor and Cam Roigard.

teams.heading: SA Rugby condemns online abuse of World Rugby officials after Erasmus ban
teams.body: In a Wednesday statement, South Africa's union cited reports of threats and abusive conduct aimed at World Rugby officials, and said it “unequivocally condemns any form of intimidation, threats, or personal attacks.” The row stems from Springboks head coach Rassie Erasmus's Monday press conference in Dublin, where he used the term “match-fixing” about unpunished foul play in the 19-21 defeat to France and earned a six-match ban. SA Rugby added that much circulating commentary and AI-generated content does not necessarily reflect the facts, before Saturday's test against Ireland.

lead.why: It is a fresh, corroborated South Africa event: SA Rugby's own statement on the fallout from the Erasmus ban.
